land.text: the coast and hinterland of present-day Puttalam: the landing 'near modern-day Mannar' (which the page takes to be the district of Chilaw), the first capital Tambapanni 'in present-day Puttalam' and the second, Upatissagama, 'seven or eight miles further north'; the page gives no boundary, so a 50 km disc on Puttalam stands for the kingdom

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Anuradhapura Kingdom'; the move to Anuradhapura is 437 BC on the infobox. Cliopatria's Anuradhapura row begins in -291, and the Anuradhapura Kingdom page of the sa-02 group may date its foundation later (Pandukabhaya, 377 BC); the pages differ.

capitals.name: Tambapanni (Puttalam)
capitals.note: Capital 'in present-day Puttalam' (Upatissa Nuwara page); first capital of the kingdom. The end year is Vijaya's death in 505 (infobox reign 543-505); the page does not date the move.

capitals.name: Upatissagama (Upatissa Nuwara)
capitals.note: 'The second capital of the Kingdom of Tambapanni ... seven or eight miles further north of the previous capital', founded by Upatissa; the start year is bridging (Upatissa's reign 505-504 on the infobox), the end is the infobox's move to Anuradhapura in 437 BC.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Anuradhapura row begins in -291). 'It existed between 543 BC and 437 BC.' The page gives no area and no boundary; the 50 km disc on Puttalam resolves to about 4,300 km2 and is a placeholder for the north-western coast around the two capitals.

ledger.note: 543 BCE: Prince Vijaya lands in Lanka and founds the Kingdom of Tambapanni. 'Sinhalese history and the historical period of Sri Lanka traditionally starts in 543 BC with the arrival of Prince Vijaya'; 'It existed between 543 BC and 437 BC'; the land 'was originally inhabited and governed by Yakkhas'. The date is the chronicle tradition the page repeats. Confidence 2 (reviewer, 2026-10-18): the Tambapanni page places the landing 'near modern-day Mannar, which is believed to be the district of Chilaw' and does not name Puttalam (only the Upatissa Nuwara page does), and the year is the chronicle tradition.

c. 505 BCE: the seat moves north to Upatissagama. The Upatissa Nuwara page (opened for this) says Upatissagama was 'the second capital' and 'established by Upatissa, a follower and senior minister of Vijaya', and gives no date; -505 is Upatissa's accession on the Tambapanni infobox.

ledger.note: 437 BCE: the kingdom's seat moves to Anuradhapura. The infobox gives the move to Anuradhapura as 437 BC and 'Succeeded by: Anuradhapura Kingdom'; 'It existed between 543 BC and 437 BC'. Confidence 2 (reviewer, 2026-10-18): the Tambapanni page places the landing 'near modern-day Mannar, which is believed to be the district of Chilaw' and does not name Puttalam (only the Upatissa Nuwara page does), and the year is the chronicle tradition.

certainty.note: A kingdom of the chronicle tradition; the pages name capitals and a landing place, not a boundary.

sources.title: Kingdom of Tambapanni
sources.note: Infobox (capital, preceded by Naga and Yakkha peoples, succeeded by Anuradhapura, reigns of Vijaya, Upatissa, Panduvasdeva, Abhaya), 543-437 BC, the landing near Mannar.

sources.title: Kingdom of Upatissa Nuwara
sources.note: Thin: Upatissagama as the second capital of Tambapanni, 7-8 miles north of the first, founded by Upatissa; no dates, no extent; not a separate state.

notes: The Upatissa Nuwara page treats Upatissagama as the second capital of Tambapanni, not a separate kingdom, so there is no Upatissa Nuwara dossier. Dates are the chronicle chronology the pages repeat (543 BC landing, 437 BC move); the Anuradhapura Kingdom page (sa-02) may say 377 BC for its founding, and Cliopatria's Anuradhapura row begins in -291, so the 437..291 span is not covered by any Cliopatria row. The kingdom's extent is not on either page; the Puttalam disc is a placeholder (a gap-filler should open the Anuradhapura Kingdom or Sri Lanka history page). Vijaya's meeting with Kuveni, the Yakkha queen, is undated and not a territorial event. The page's infobox says 'Succeeded by: Anuradhapura Kingdom' but 'Preceded by' the Naga and Yakkha peoples, who are not states here. Gazetteer: Upatissagama (8.14N 79.85E) and Chilaw are not places; the gazetteer's name for Puttalam is 'Puttalan'.
